case_name: Technical Employees' Association of Railways and another v Ministry of Railways and others
petitioner: Technical Employees' Association of Railways and another
facts: The Technical Employees' Association of Railways through its President is the petitioner here assailing the validity of circular dated 28-9-1998 issued by the Railway Board.

Employees of the Railways are from different parts of the country. The circular in question which is being assailed provides that for promotion from the post of Khalasi the higher qualification of matriculation and ITI pass should be achieved.
Khalasi who are already in service, did not possess the aforesaid qualification and if such a circular is allowed to operate, there will be stagnation
The impugned circular be quashed being hit by Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India.
issues: Whether prescribing higher qualification for the purpose of promotion is permissible under law
petitioner_arguments: Khalasi who are already in service, did not possess the aforesaid qualification and if such a circular is allowed to operate, there will be stagnation
The impugned circular be quashed being hit by Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India
respondent_arguments: It would be open for the employer to prescribe qualifications both for direct recruitment as well as for promotion
Prescribing such qualifications cannot be held to be arbitrary or irrational
court_reasoning: For maintaining efficiency of service, the higher qualification is required for discharge of the duties in the higher positions
The Board has issued circular in consonance with the recommendation of the Pay Commission
holding: The writ petition is accordingly dismissed.
cases_cited: As early as in the case of Union of India v. S.B
Technical Employees' Association of Railways and another v Ministry of Railways
and the decision of this Court in T.R. Kothandaraman v. T.N
